CHROMIUM: Bluetooth: increase LE auto connection timeout to 5 seconds This changes the LE auto connection timeout from 2 seconds to 5 seconds in order to improve the connection successful rate in a noisy environment with the most common use case for Chromeb* - audio streaming via Wi-Fi. In the experiment, the LE connection attempts to a remote Android phone (1000 times) were performed when the DUT was connected to a pair of Bluetooth headphone and streamed audio via Wi-Fi. The observation is that ~1.5% of the LE connection attempts took more than 2 seconds to complete, and the max time is around 3.5 seconds. Therefore, 5 is selected to be the timeout. BUG=None TEST=perform LE connection test for 1000 times with an Android phone while streaming audio via Wi-Fi and through a pair of Bluetooth headphone Change-Id: I545e74ac75db18cc4b7a9c05880c9765af77585c Signed-off-by: Miao-chen Chou <mcchou@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1000097 Reviewed-by: Sukumar Ghorai <sukumar.ghorai@intel.com> Reviewed-by: Dmitry Grinberg <dmitrygr@google.com> (cherry picked from commit 0c4adb227387a5648172509db93ce0ce554cf2ca) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1013000

tast: Refactor test-listing code. Move test-printing functionality out of the cmd/tast/run package and into listCmd in cmd/tast. cmd/tast/run now takes a Mode enum that specifies whether it should run or list tests, and ListTestsMode returns tests via a slice of TestResult structs, the same as RunTestsMode. This will make it possible to update the list command to merge both local and remote tests instead of only listing one type or the other. BUG=chromium:831849 TEST=updated unit tests; also verified that "tast run" and "tast list" work as before Change-Id: I7c1a92ef34cc8c4825c7aa00b663e713e2a380fa Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1011147 Commit-Ready: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Tested-by: Dan Erat <derat@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Jason Clinton <jclinton@chromium.org>

cryptohome: preserve mount-encrypted logs over reboots In addition to creating a new /var/log/mount-encrypted.log for each boot, dump its contents into syslog, so that it's possible to see mount-encrypted logs from previous boots in /var/log/messages.
